  "In view of the Skywalk Construction work at Mehdipatnam Rythu Bazar bus stop, and Secunderabad bus stop side there will be traffic diversion and alternate routes on the intervening nights of 14/15.04.2026 and 15/16.04.2026 from 0000 hours to 0600 hours to ensure free flow of traffic and to avoid traffic congestion.* 

TRAFFIC DIVERSIONS AND ALTERNATIVE ROUTES 

1.On intervening night of 14/15.04.2026 and 15/16.04.2026: Traffic coming from Masab Tank, NMDC, S.D Eye Hospital towards Rethibowli-Nanal Nagar will be diverted at PVNR Expressway, Pillar No.2 & 3 (Azizia Mosque) towards Meraj Cafe-Right-Mehdipatnam (at Pillar No. 15) and will be merged in the regular route. 

2. On intervening night of 15/16.04.2026: Traffic coming from Tolichowki, Langerhouse & Attapur via., Nanal Nagar-Rethibowli towards Masab Tank will be diverted at PVNR Expressway Pillar No.23 'U' turn to the opposite direction and will be allowed to merge in the same direction at Pillar No.4&5 in the regular route.

Commuters are appealed to follow traffic updates on our social media platform @ Hyderabad Traffic Police face book page (https://t.co/RMgFu4sqLB) and @ HYDTP (Twitter handle). In case of any emergency in travel, kindly call our traffic help line 9010203626 for travel assistance.

 All citizens are requested to make note of the above traffic congestion and diversion, take alternate routes to reach your destinations and cooperate with the Hyderabad Traffic Police.

Jt. Commissioner of Police, 
Traffic, Hyderabad.

data.text:
Real life went full anime… 😳

Two intense real-life moments that got viral online after fans noticed how closely they resemble iconic anime scenes.

The first image shows a protester in the Philippines clashing with riot police, captured mid-kick in a moment that strongly copy the fighting style and pose of Luffy from One Piece. The angle, movement, and even the straw hat added by fans made it look straight out of an anime scene.

The second image features a monk confronting police during a protest in Thailand. His stance and motion quickly drew comparisons to Aang from Avatar: The Last Airbender, with many pointing out the calm yet powerful energy in the moment that mirrors the character’s fighting style.

While both images come from serious real-world situations involving protests and civil unrest, the internet couldn’t help but notice how these split-second moments looked like something straight out of anime.

The war killed my job.

This is definitely a sentence I never thought I’d say, but here we are.

It’s unfortunate that the escalating tensions in the Middle East didn’t just impact economies, travel, and investor confidence, but it also quietly wiped out opportunities, teams, and months of work behind the scenes. Mine included.

Over the past few months, I had the opportunity to help build toward something genuinely exciting with @planxconf in Dubai this April. The vision was to bring together 3,000 high-growth founders from around the world and create the kind of room where ideas, capital, partnerships, and life-changing conversations could actually happen.

We were building with serious momentum. The lineup included names like @StevenBartlett , @DanielPriestley, @simonsquibb, @ysiu , and more. We were also working with incredible partners like @brincvc, @EntrepreneurMAG, @MillionaireMigr, @TheBlockCo  and others who believed in what this could become and everyone was all in.

When the opportunity was first presented to me by Wilbound led by Logan Merrick and Maricris Valencia, I was already excited, and after meeting the man behind the vision, Frankie Ngo, and seeing how big this could really be, I knew this was the kind of thing you throw yourself into fully. It felt meaningful. It felt timely. It felt like we were about to build something that could truly make a dent.

And that’s the thing about building at a global level: sometimes the strategy is right, the team is excellent, the timing feels perfect, and you still get hit by forces way bigger than you.

Of course, I’m disappointed as anyone would be, but I’m also clear about my mission.

This chapter reminded me what I’m actually great at, which is knowing how to build rooms people want to be in. I know how to connect founders, creators, investors, and ecosystems in ways that create real impact, as clearly shown in building the @foundersrc  Manila Chapter and @joinopenverse  builders community. I know how to turn a big vision into something people can believe in, buy into, and rally behind, like what I did in cofounding the civic tech movement https://t.co/5e9hcgEr2L.

And while I’m in this in-between season, I’m not sitting still. I’m exploring what’s next, sharpening my knowledge, and paying close attention to where the biggest opportunities are forming. I’m spending time deepening my understanding of AI, trends, growth, and the very obvious gaps in the market across founder communities, startup ecosystems, tech events, and global expansion programs.

There’s a lot that’s broken in how we build for founders today, and I want to be part of building what comes next.

In the coming days, I will be building micro-startups like viral apps and SaaS to develop a new framework to revolutionize and replace incubators and accelerators with something more robust, relevant, and revenue-driven.

Keen to co-create? DM is open. Let's build! 🚀
